chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who had an umm walad, and her child from him died. Then he married her to another man, and she bore him a child. Then that man died, and she returned to her master. So does he have the right to be intimate with her before marrying her?
He must not be intimate with her until she completes the waiting period for the deceased husband, which is four months and ten days. Then he may be intimate with her by ownership, without nikah.
I said: What about her child from the husband? He said: If he left wealth, the child is to be purchased from it at the assessed value, then freed, and made to inherit.
I said: If he left no wealth? He said: Then the child remains with his mother in the same condition as her.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: The prescribed waiting period for a widow in this case.
key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: A slave woman who has borne a child to her master.
key_terms.بِالْقِيمَةِ: At assessed value or market valuation.
key_terms.بِالْمِلْكِ: By right of ownership rather than through marriage.
key_terms.تَعْتَدَّ: To observe the waiting period ('iddah) required after the husband's death.
key_terms.وَ وُرِّثَ: Then he is made to inherit.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an umm walad who returns to her master after her husband's death, and what happens to her child?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about an umm walad who was married off by her master, then returned to him after her husband's death. It states that she must first observe the waiting period of four months and ten days, after which her master may be intimate with her by ownership without nikah. It also explains the legal status of her child from the deceased husband in relation to wealth, emancipation, and inheritance.
